parts.title: Rules of the Room
parts.text: The regional debate tournament began on a gray Saturday, and Alicia felt her stomach tighten as the **moderator** tapped the microphone and explained the rules. Each team would defend a **stance** on whether every student should perform community service. Her partner, Rohan, whispered that judges rewarded speeches that were **concise**, so they had trimmed their notes down to a single page.

parts.title: The Showman
parts.text: Their first opponent was Simone, who was famous for her **oratory**. She spoke with perfect **inflection**, lifting her voice on key facts and dropping it for warnings, and the audience leaned forward. Her teammate was the opposite. He opened with a **bombastic** flourish, all thunder and sweeping gestures, then slid into a **tirade** that mocked the whole idea of service without offering a single fact.

parts.title: The Answer
parts.text: When Alicia rose, she did not shout. She built a **cogent** case, linking each statistic to a clear conclusion. Her rivals tried to **discredit** her sources by calling them biased, but she calmly produced the originals. Rohan, who was usually **cynical** about judges, was startled by how closely the room listened. He grew **vehement** only once, during the rebuttal, insisting that learning to help strangers was worth more than any trophy. At lunch, Alicia and Simone discovered an easy **rapport**, trading tips about nerves and note cards.

parts.title: After the Final
parts.text: Their team did not take home the trophy, but the score sheets told a different story. The judges had praised honest evidence over loud theatrics. Alicia realized that persuasion works best when people feel respected instead of attacked. On the ride home, Rohan admitted that he wanted to keep debating, not to beat anyone, but to learn how to disagree well.

definitions.meaning1: Clear, logical and convincing. Example: The lawyer made a cogent argument that persuaded the jury.

definitions.meaning1: Giving a lot of information in few words. Example: Keep your summary concise; one paragraph is enough.

definitions.meaning1: The art of speaking in public in a skillful and powerful way. Example: The student council president was admired for her oratory.

definitions.meaning1: Showing strong, intense feeling; forceful. Example: She gave a vehement denial when she was accused of cheating.

definitions.meaning1: To damage the reputation of someone, or to make something seem untrue or unreliable. Example: The scientist tried to discredit the rumor with clear evidence.
definitions.meaning2: Loss of respect or good reputation. Example: His careless behavior brought discredit on the whole team.
definitions.studentChallenge: The rival candidate tried to ___ her by spreading rumors.

definitions.meaning1: Using grand, showy words that sound important but mean very little. Example: The bombastic announcer promised the greatest show in the history of the universe.
definitions.studentChallenge: His ___ speech was full of loud words but few ideas.

definitions.meaning1: A friendly, understanding relationship in which people communicate easily. Example: The new teacher quickly built rapport with her class.
definitions.studentChallenge: The two partners developed an easy ___ after months of working together.

definitions.meaning1: Distrustful of people's motives; believing that people act only out of selfishness. Example: Cynical about advertising, he assumed every claim was a trick.
definitions.studentChallenge: She grew ___ about promises after being let down so many times.

definitions.meaning1: A change in the pitch or tone of the voice while speaking. Example: The question was clear from the rising inflection in her voice.
definitions.meaning2: A change in the form of a word to show tense, number or other meaning. Example: The ending -ed is an inflection that shows past tense in English.
definitions.studentChallenge: You could hear the excitement in the ___ of her voice.

definitions.meaning1: A person who leads a discussion or debate, keeping order and making sure the rules are followed. Example: The moderator reminded each speaker to stay within the time limit.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ asked the audience to hold their questions until the end.

definitions.meaning1: A person's stated position or opinion on an issue. Example: The mayor took a firm stance against closing the library.
definitions.meaning2: The way a person stands, especially in sports. Example: The batter shifted into a wide stance and waited for the pitch.
